# NodeMangler

> Free, open-source node-based image editor and procedural texture generator written in Rust. A Substance Designer / Material Maker alternative that is not built on a game engine. Desktop GUI plus a headless CLI that share the same JSON graph format, designed to be easy for scripts and LLMs to drive.

Key facts (as of v1.0.7, 2026-08-01):

- 443 nodes across 6 categories — Images (213), Numbers (104), Colors (53), Text (26), Curves (25), Logic (22) — plus subgraph nodes for packaging a pipeline into one reusable node.
- 47 procedural noise generators (basic, fractal, cellular, structural, grunge, process) plus a simulation category (hydraulic erosion, river meandering, hillslope diffusion, and more).
- Photo-editing suite: camera raw development (CR3/NEF/ARW/DNG), shadow/highlight recovery, 8-band HSL mixer, tone mapping (Reinhard/ACES/filmic), 3-way color grading, tone equalizer, Kelvin white balance with Bradford adaptation, luma/chroma denoise, lens distortion + chromatic aberration correction, and per-channel curves.
- PBR material authoring: normal / AO / curvature / bevel from height maps, a live 3D material preview, and channel-packed export presets for Godot, Unity, and Unreal.
- 14 color spaces (sRGB, Linear RGB, HSL, HSV, HWB, Lab, LCH, Oklab, Oklch, CMYK, XYZ, xyY, YCbCr, YUV) and 17 blend modes.
- 17 image file formats, including HEIC/HEIF read (iPhone photos) via a pure-Rust decoder, JPEG XL and PSD read, and AVIF / OpenEXR / Radiance HDR write.
- Tethered shooting: watch a folder and automatically develop + export each new photo as it lands (the camera transport is handled by EOS Utility/gphoto2/Lightroom; NodeMangler watches the download folder).
- Camera raw development (read-only) via rawler: Canon CR3/CR2, Nikon NEF, Sony ARW, Fujifilm RAF, Adobe DNG and ~20 more, with demosaic, as-shot or neutral white balance, sRGB or scene-linear output, and EXIF orientation applied.
- Floating-point pipeline: images stay 1–4 channel f32 from input to output; conversion happens only at I/O.
- Resolution-independent spatial parameters: design at 512px, render at 4K, same relative result.
- Batch runs: sweep a folder of images through a graph, saving outputs per file.
- Runs on Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), and Linux. Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Graphs are plain JSON files (`.mangler.json`). The CLI (`mangler_cli`) runs them headless: build a graph in the GUI, then automate it from scripts or agents.

## Docs

- [Full node reference and README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dan335/nodemangler/main/README.md): always-current list of every node, organized by category
- [Source code](https://github.com/dan335/nodemangler): GitHub repository (Rust, Cargo workspace under `app/`)

## Download

- [Latest release](https://github.com/dan335/nodemangler/releases/latest): prebuilt binaries for Windows, macOS, and Linux, plus a Linux AppImage and SHA256SUMS.txt
- [itch.io page](https://danp.itch.io/nodemangler): alternative download; the itch.io desktop app auto-updates its installs
- Homebrew (macOS/Linux): `brew tap dan335/nodemangler https://github.com/dan335/nodemangler && brew install nodemangler` — installs the GUI as `nodemangler` and the CLI as `mangle`
- Scoop (Windows): `scoop bucket add nodemangler https://github.com/dan335/nodemangler && scoop install nodemangler`
